title: Continuous assurance, engineered
lead: From service scope to a defensible readiness decision.
points: A fictional multi-cloud service inspired by a TechGRC compliance role.
Runnable control tests, explicit evidence limits and a phased implementation handbook.
Synthetic data throughout the public demonstration.
notes: Open the dashboard and distinguish locally tested functionality from the proposed production architecture.

title: Start with the business decision
lead: What does the service need to demonstrate?
points: Understand obligations and service commitments.
Find control failures and missing evidence early.
Give management and assessors traceable, reviewable information.
notes: The consultant coordinates under the TechGRC manager. Management owns risk acceptance and independent assessors own their conclusions.

title: Scope before score
lead: The denominator is an assurance control.
points: Inventory accounts, subscriptions, projects, resources and dependencies.
Map datasets, replicas, backups, exports and telemetry.
Retain missing and deleted resources in the relevant population.
notes: Show the ninth synthetic asset, which is absent from evidence but remains in scope.

title: Classification becomes a control input
lead: Sensitivity alone is not the whole data contract.
points: Define purpose, owner, residency, retention and criticality.
Validate discovery coverage and have owners approve classifications.
Protect metadata changes and test actual enforcement.
notes: Explain resource tags versus Purview labels, Resource Manager tags and BigQuery policy tags.

title: A complete evidence chain
lead: Every conclusion has an identifiable path.
points: Requirement → risk → control → implementation.
Test → evidence → finding → corrective action.
Independent retest → management decision.
notes: Use the architecture diagram in the handbook. Describe separate collection, storage and approval trust boundaries.

title: Deliver in eight phases
lead: Finish one vertical slice before expanding.
points: Charter, discover, design controls, secure the platform.
Automate a slice, prove process operation, remediate and prepare audit.
Operate with evidence-quality and collection SLOs.
notes: Planning ranges are assumptions. Discovery and legal constraints can change the sequence.

title: AWS implementation
lead: Use services available to a new lab account.
points: Config and service APIs for scoped configuration evidence.
CloudTrail, EventBridge and protected S3 for collection and custody.
Macie where appropriate, with explicit coverage limits.
notes: AWS Audit Manager is not a new-customer baseline after April 30, 2026. Distinguish template authorship from live deployment.

title: Azure implementation
lead: Join configuration, identity and data governance evidence.
points: Resource Graph and Policy Insights for resource/control state.
Entra evidence and monitored diagnostics for process operation.
Purview supported scans plus tested enforcement paths.
notes: Azure Policy native percentages differ from the strict pass metric. Private endpoints and public-access settings are separate checks.

title: Google Cloud implementation
lead: Keep labels, policy and data controls distinct.
points: Cloud Asset Inventory and API contracts for scope and facts.
Cloud Audit Logs, Cloud Storage and BigQuery for evidence flow.
Review Compliance Manager scope, residency and encryption constraints.
notes: The narrow adapter returns unknown for inherited public-access prevention until policy evidence is available.

title: Good, better, best
lead: Match complexity to a documented requirement.
points: Good: reviewed registers and repeatable tests.
Better: reconciled collection, policy checks and integrated remediation.
Best: trusted provenance, regional custody and sustained quality.
notes: These are architecture maturity options, not provider product tiers. More tools do not automatically create stronger assurance.

title: Identity and SDLC
lead: Operating evidence connects people and changes to effective access.
points: Joiner, mover and leaver reconciliation includes actual revocation.
Privileged access needs effective-policy and session evidence.
Production deployments reconcile to approvals and artifact identities.
notes: Supplied process booleans in the fixture are not a substitute for authenticated HR, IdP, ITSM and pipeline integrations.

title: Recovery must be demonstrated
lead: A successful backup job is only one input.
points: Approve RPO and RTO through business impact analysis.
Recover representative data and dependencies in an isolated environment.
Measure elapsed time, recoverable data age and integrity.
notes: Show the synthetic seven-hour restore against the four-hour lab target. The target is a project choice, not a universal framework requirement.

title: Four states, no hidden uncertainty
lead: Unknown evidence remains visible.
points: PASS: all defined predicates satisfied. FAIL: a demonstrated violation.
UNKNOWN: missing, stale, malformed or future evidence.
NOT_APPLICABLE: outside a documented control population.
notes: Known failures remain failures when another predicate is unknown. Accepted risk annotates a failure instead of changing its state.

title: The reproducible result
lead: One dataset drives the report and dashboard.
points: 9 assets × 14 controls = 126 evaluated pairs.
87 PASS · 9 FAIL · 12 UNKNOWN · 18 NOT_APPLICABLE.
88.89% evaluated coverage and 80.56% passing share of applicable pairs.
notes: These counts describe the fixed synthetic fixture. They are not organizational compliance results or a risk-weighted score.

title: Proof lives in the failure tests
lead: The code must handle conditions that create false assurance.
points: Missing resources, stale timestamps and invalid types.
Expired/self-approved exceptions and incomplete provider fields.
Changed evidence files detected against the local manifest.
notes: Run the unit suite and demonstrate one mutation. Explain that the hash manifest is not an authenticated signature.

title: Remediation reaches the cause
lead: A closed ticket is not a completed control.
points: Validate criteria, condition, population and impact.
Test causal hypotheses and fix reusable templates/processes.
Recollect independently and verify effectiveness before closure.
notes: Preserve original findings and evidence. Separate immediate containment from preventive work.

title: Frameworks keep their own meaning
lead: Reuse evidence without claiming equivalence.
points: SOC 2: scoped service controls and engagement evidence.
ISO 27001: an operating management system and risk treatment.
PCI DSS, HIPAA and HITRUST: distinct applicability and assessment workstreams.
notes: The handbook provides thematic mapping and implementation workstreams, not a complete licensed certification workbook.

title: Global operation and human controls
lead: Cloud posture does not cover the entire program.
points: Acknowledged handoffs, regional evidence custody and named decision owners.
Supplier, personnel, physical, policy and privacy responsibilities.
Management reporting that exposes unknowns and overdue decisions.
notes: Describe how the same evidence supports engineering, business and assessor audiences at different levels of detail.

title: AI is an optional assistant
lead: Keep evidence and authority outside unconstrained model output.
points: Draft summaries and candidate mappings from approved sources.
Test citation accuracy, unsupported claims and prompt injection.
Retain deterministic states and human approval for consequential decisions.
notes: No model APIs are called by the demo. Agentic workflows are a proposed extension with bounded tools and reviewed access.

title: Seven projects from the role's priorities
lead: Each priority in the hiring notes became runnable work with expected results.
points: Use cases, configuration drift, control evaluation and evidence data flows.
Remediation verification, audit process testing and SOC 2-first coverage.
Every project carries provider-native fixtures for AWS, Azure and GCP.
notes: Open the projects page. Each card shows the role priority it answers, the headline result and the downloadable bundle. The base lab tests supplied facts; the projects test where those facts come from.

title: Derive the fact, then test the test
lead: A control result should come from source records, and its logic should catch known faults.
points: Eight use cases join HR, identity, CI/CD, backup, scanner and cloud records: 21 pass, 21 fail, 8 unknown.
An IdP-only leaver check passes a worker whose AWS access key stayed active.
109 seeded faults: production logic catches all, four weaker candidates each miss several.
notes: Walk through worker W-1005 in Project 01, then the naive leaver candidate in Project 03. The point is that a plausible control can look fine on clean data and still hide exceptions. Note that the same author wrote the vectors, so independent review of the vectors matters.

title: Follow the evidence to the control
lead: A pass on incomplete or altered data is not a pass.
points: Four pipelines reconciled hop by hop: three defective, one reliable.
A dropped UTC offset turned a 27.5-hour removal into an apparent 22-hour pass.
One storage baseline across three clouds, with drift classified by change record.
notes: Show DF-04 in Project 04, then the recomputed W-1004 result. Then show the unauthorized change to aws-records-01 in Project 02 and the matching CloudTrail event the SIEM never received in DF-01.

title: Close on evidence, and test the audit itself
lead: Remediation and audit work have their own failure modes.
points: Closure needs independent, sustained retests and a fix at the source: 1 of 6 findings is eligible.
Automatic remediation looped against an approved change and touched an exempt bucket.
A sample of 25 found 1 of 3 planted deviations. Testing every item found all 3.
notes: Use Project 05 to show why a single passing screenshot does not close a finding. Use Project 06 to show population reconciliation before sampling, then sampling risk next to full-population testing. Close with the SOC 2 coverage backlog from Project 07.

title: A practical path to production
lead: The next stage is a measured pilot.
points: Choose one service, one provider and a small control set.
Authenticate sources, validate semantics and prove live integration.
Expand after evidence quality, ownership and operating cost are understood.
notes: Close with the source download, handbook and runnable commands. Do not claim live cloud implementation or an external audit outcome.
